I wrote /app/bin/crosstabs.py and ran it on /app/data. The output is saved at /app/out/tables.json. It uses only the standard library, and I didn't touch data, docs, tests or tools.

- Unit tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ran 4 tests and they all passed.
- Approved tables: python tools/check_tables.py reported that every figure matches, in the summary and in all six tables.

I implemented the rules from the notes rather than anything specific to the current files. I haven't run it on any survey beyond the four test fixtures and the current data.

/app/STATUS.json is written with status success.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | head -100; cat docs/overview.md; wc -c docs/*
cd /app/docs; cat exports.md codebook.md cleaning.md weighting.md tables.md output.md changelog.md
cd /app/docs; sed -n '/^## 5. Routing/,$p' codebook.md; cat cleaning.md; cat weighting.md

cd /app; cat data/codebook.json | head -150; cat data/weighting.json data/tables.json data/exports/export_log.txt; head -c 600 data/exports/*.csv; cat tools/check_tables.py | head -60; cat tests/test_tables.py

cd /app; python3 - <<'E'
import json
c=json.load(open('data/codebook.json'))
for q in c['questions'][2:]:
    print(json.dumps(q))
E
file data/exports/*; cat data/exports/export_log.txt | head -3
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/crosstabs.py data out/tables.json; echo $?; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; python tools/check_tables.py

cd /app; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/crosstabs.py implementing the documented reading, cleaning, routing, raking/trimming and crosstab rules, and generated /app/out/tables.json. The unit tests pass and tools/check_tables.py reports every figure matches."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
